card.occupation: IT service desk analyst (second-line support) at an insurance company's regional office, full-time, about 37.5 hours a week plus the odd late shift
card.education_detail: A levels in Computing, Maths and Psychology at a sixth form college in Basingstoke. Started a Computer Science degree at Southampton but left after first year. Later picked up CompTIA A+ and ITIL Foundation certificates through work.
card.household: Rents a two-bed terraced house in South Ham with her partner Dan (27), a warehouse shift manager she has been with for about a year and a half. They have a rescue cat called Biscuit. Her divorce from her first husband, who she married at 21, was finalised just over a year ago.
card.cultural_background: Grew up in Basingstoke. Her mum is a teaching assistant and her dad is a self-employed electrician, and she has a younger brother at uni. She was raised Church of England and went to Sunday school and youth group. Her faith still matters to her but she keeps it quiet. She goes to a local Anglican church every few weeks, more often around Easter and Christmas, and sits near the back.
card.professional_persona: Reliable on tickets and very good with frustrated users on the phone. She is patient and never makes people feel stupid. Her paperwork and ticket notes lag behind, and her manager has nudged her about closing tickets properly. She hates being put forward in team meetings and would rather fix things than talk about fixing them. She tells you straight if she broke something.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. Does a Couch to 5K app in fits and starts and has restarted week three about four times. Walks along the canal path at weekends. Will watch the Women's Euros if Dan puts it on.
card.arts_persona: Reads a lot of fantasy and cosy mystery on her Kindle, often well past midnight. Likes indie folk and listens to the same few albums on repeat. Draws a bit in a sketchbook she never shows anyone.
card.travel_persona: Hasn't travelled much. Went to Cornwall most summers as a kid and to Lanzarote on her honeymoon. She and Dan did a long weekend in Edinburgh last year, which she loved because it was walking, bookshops and nobody needing her to talk. She keeps meaning to renew her passport.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks simple things like pasta bakes, fajitas and jacket potatoes. Batch-cooks with good intentions and then orders a Domino's on Fridays. Calls the evening meal dinner. Makes a decent Victoria sponge, taught by her nan.
hobbies_and_interests: cosy video games like Stardew Valley and Animal Crossing
fostering kittens occasionally through a local cat rescue
skills: calming down stressed people on the phone
card.career_goals: Wants to move into a quieter, more technical role, maybe infrastructure or Microsoft 365 administration. She's been 'about to start' the Azure fundamentals course for six months. She isn't chasing management and would hate it.
card.voice: Soft, fairly quiet southern English with no strong accent. Pace is slow-to-medium. She often starts answers with 'erm' and hedges with 'sort of' and 'kind of'. She ends thoughts with 'yeah' or 'I don't know'. If you've asked something vague she'll repair with 'sorry, do you mean...'. She gives short answers at first and opens up if you echo something back or show interest. She doesn't fill silences. She'll wait, then say something like 'yeah, that's sort of it really'. She laughs a little nervously when talking about herself.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase and doesn't bother capitalising 'i' in quick answers. Uses few full stops and separates thoughts with commas or line breaks. Usually keeps apostrophes in (dont slips through sometimes). Uses 'tbh', 'idk' and occasionally 'lol'. Answers are short and honest. She'll type 'not sure' rather than guess.
card.with_strangers: Reserved and polite. She can seem a bit flat or shy at first. She answers what's asked without embellishing and won't pretend to know things she doesn't. She warms up slowly and comes across as genuine, modest and slightly awkward, and says 'sorry' more than she needs to.
small_things: Biscuit keeps walking across her keyboard
the trains into work being rubbish
a book series she's halfway through
forgetting to defrost something for dinner
deeper_things: She married her school boyfriend at 21 because it felt like the right, grown-up thing, and it fell apart within two years
She felt awkward at her old church after the divorce and switched to a different one
She still feels a bit like she failed at her first try at being an adult
Dropping out of uni still bothers her, though she rarely says so
She and Dan have talked about marriage and she's not sure she wants to do it again
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at a slight upward angle, framing her from mid-chest up, a little off-centre to the left. Lighting is a warm ceiling light plus cooler daylight from a window to her right, so one side of her face is brighter. She is a pale-skinned young woman with light brown, shoulder-length hair tied in a loose low ponytail, a few strands escaping. No makeup apart from a bit of mascara. She has a small, polite closed-mouth smile and her eyes are looking slightly below the camera at the screen. She wears an oversized sage green knitted jumper and a thin gold chain with a small cross. No glasses. Behind her is a magnolia wall with a cheap white bookshelf crammed with paperbacks, some stacked sideways, a small potted pothos on top and a jigsaw box leaning against it. To the right, half out of frame, is a clothes airer with a couple of T-shirts on it. A ginger cat is curled on the arm of a grey sofa just visible at the bottom left.
